questions.q: Why is there no single "lifecycle stage" column that summarizes a transaction's entire journey?
options: Because Oracle Fusion has no status columns at all
Because only AR transactions have lifecycles
Because transactions don't actually have stages
Because each stage (entered, validated, accounted, posted, paid) leaves evidence in different tables, not one unified column
questions.explain: A transaction's lifecycle is recorded across multiple tables — header status, payment tables, posting indicators — not consolidated into one column.

questions.q: What does the status column on AP_INVOICES_ALL actually tell you?
options: The ledger's functional currency
Whether the invoice has been fully paid
The validation/accounting state of the invoice header, not its payment state
The customer's credit limit
questions.explain: The AP invoice header status reflects validation and accounting state; payment state is a separate fact tracked in AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL.

questions.q: In AR_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL, which is the more authoritative signal of whether a transaction is truly settled: the STATUS column or the amount-due-remaining figure?
options: The amount-due-remaining figure, since STATUS can say OPEN even when only a tiny leftover balance remains
Neither column is reliable
Only the invoice header status matters
The STATUS column alone is always sufficient
questions.explain: The numeric amount-due-remaining value is the authoritative signal; a transaction can show STATUS = OPEN while carrying only a small residual balance.

questions.q: What does "posting status" refer to, as distinct from payment status?
options: Whether a supplier's address has been verified
Whether a subledger transaction's accounting has actually been transferred to the General Ledger
Whether a customer has a credit hold
Whether an invoice number is a duplicate
questions.explain: Posting status tracks the subledger-to-GL handoff — a separate axis entirely from whether the transaction has been paid or applied.

questions.q: What is the recommended habit when encountering an unfamiliar status or flag column?
options: Ignore status columns entirely
Always assume a status column tracks payment state
Assume it means the same thing as a similarly-named column on a different table
Identify which table and row-level concept the column belongs to, then confirm against its documented description
questions.explain: Checking which table a status column lives on, what that table represents, and its documented description avoids the kind of confusion this lesson covers.
